svg.title: How an editor's page in the CMS becomes a rendered page
svg.desc: A top-to-bottom map of one page render. An editor arranges blocks in the Payload admin, which stores them as a layout array on a Pages document. When a visitor asks for a route, the server component fetches everything it needs in parallel through the Local API, which runs in process rather than over HTTP. Site settings are cached for five minutes under a tag; the collection queries are not. The fetched documents are handed to the block renderer as a single data bundle, so an editor adding blocks cannot change how many queries the page runs. The renderer switches on each block's type and returns the matching section component. Ten block types are defined and all ten are handled. If no page document exists for the route, the page falls back to a default composition built from the collections, and only when those are empty too does it show the empty-page notice.
